quizName: Hardest Questions in North dakota Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: Where should you find the best information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who rides a different type of motorcycle
A television show about motorcycle riding

questions.explanation: Read your owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual explains your specific motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that fits snugly
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that fits snugly is the single most effective thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Regularly, as part of your normal riding routine
Never, because other drivers can see you

questions.correctAnswerText: Regularly, as part of your normal riding routine
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to know what is behind you. This should be part of your normal riding routine for safety.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery and hard to control a motorcycle on?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all slippery. Ride with extra caution on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need regular checks?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chain, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. A small mechanical problem on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane
It is better than going too slowly
You will stay in your lane
It is okay because motorcycles are small

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to drift into another lane or off the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: How can you reduce your risk of an accident?

options.text: Blend in with traffic and avoid being noticed
Use turn signals only at night
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning
Follow the vehicle ahead very closely

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning
questions.explanation: To reduce accident risk, be visible to others. Use your turn signals, brake light, and position yourself well. Keep safe distance from other vehicles, watch ahead, and be ready for hazards.

questions.question: What should be your main source of information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual as your main source. It has information about your specific motorcycle's features, operation, and maintenance.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: The same as a face shield

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle fit you properly?

options.text: When your feet can touch the ground while seated
When you can reach the controls by stretching
When the handlebars go over your head
When your feet cannot reach the foot pegs

questions.correctAnswerText: When your feet can touch the ground while seated
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can reach the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to easily reach and use all the controls.

questions.question: Your body can only remove alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body. There are no shortcuts to sobering up.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.
Be close to the road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Encourage them to take less-crowded roads.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking. Do everything you can to stop them. Get a group of friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may drive slowly while looking for a spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver may pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. People may step out from between cars.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Protective clothing includes sturdy jackets, long pants, boots that cover your ankles, and gloves. A stocking cap is not protective gear.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Encourage them to take quieter roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking. Stop them by taking their keys if needed. Arrange another way for them to get home.

questions.question: Which color helps you be seen while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible. Wear bright colors any time you ride, day or night.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your alcohol level. They may keep you awake, but they cannot make you sober.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are not very important since motorcycles are small.
Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Should not be used if no vehicles are nearby.
Are harder to use than on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a rider, you are at risk. Always use your turn signals to warn others before you turn or change lanes, even if no one appears to be nearby.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Boots that go over the ankle
A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots that support your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not protect you.

questions.question: If wearing footwear with laces, the laces:

options.text: Should be taken off the footwear.

questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoe laces while riding. Loose laces can get caught on your motorcycle.

questions.question: As a motorcycle operator, you can help others see you by:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be more visible. Always use your headlight and turn signals.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can improve their visibility by:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Always use your headlight, signals, and brake light.

questions.question: Which types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly as part of normal riding. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.
